issues.description: Class Bitmap24 constructor is declared with different parameter types between the template header and the template implementation. In the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the constructor is declared as Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height) but the template implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository header (solution example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). This long vs int mismatch between declaration and definition produces different mangled signatures and will lead to a linker error (undefined reference to the declared constructor) or confusing behavior for students comparing template and solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across header and implementation. Update the template header declaration to use int parameters to match the implementation and the solution: change 'Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height);' to 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);'. Alternatively, if long is required for a specific reason, change the implementation (and solution) to use long everywhere — but the recommended fix is to align the template header to 'int' to match the implementation and solution provided.
